# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 59

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 59:1 "give me your whole heart and mind" vs. "give me your complete attention"

- **EMET:** "give me your whole heart and mind"
- **LOGOS:** "give me your complete attention of heart and mind"
- **PNEUMA:** "give me your full attention — heart and mind"
- **Greek:** *dos moi kardian holēn sou kai noun* — give me your whole heart and mind
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "give me your complete attention of heart and mind" (LOGOS). "Complete attention" smooths the idiom; "heart and mind" is preserved as the biblical anthropological pair.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 59:2 "brought them to perfection and empowered them" vs. "brought them to completion and empowered them"

- **EMET:** "brought them to perfection and empowered them"
- **LOGOS:** "brought them to completion and empowered them"
- **PNEUMA:** "brought it to completion and gave it power"
- **Greek:** *teleiosas...edynāmōsen* — brought to completion/perfection...empowered
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "brought them to completion and empowered them" (LOGOS). *Teleioō* = complete/perfect; "completion" avoids the eschatological connotation of "perfection."

---

## Disagreement 3 — 59:2 "vine is this people that he planted" vs. "vine is the people"

- **EMET:** "the vine is this people that he planted"
- **LOGOS:** "the vine is the people whom he planted"
- **PNEUMA:** "The vine is the people God planted"
- **Note:** Minor variation only.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the vine is the people whom he planted" (LOGOS). "Whom" is appropriate for people; PNEUMA adds "God" which is explanatory but not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 59:2 "fences are the holy angels...who protect" vs. "who keep"

- **EMET:** "the holy angels of the Lord who protect his people"
- **LOGOS:** "the holy angels of the Lord who keep his people"
- **PNEUMA:** "the holy angels of the Lord who protect his people"
- **Greek:** *oi phroūrontes ton laon* — who guard/keep the people
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the holy angels of the Lord who keep his people" (LOGOS). *Phrourein* = to keep/guard in the sense of ongoing protection; both "protect" and "keep" are accurate.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 59:2 "transgressions" vs. "sins" vs. "weeds = sins"

- **EMET:** "the transgressions of the servants of God"
- **LOGOS:** "the transgressions of the servants of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "the sins of God's servants"
- **Greek:** *hai anomiai tōn doulōn* — the lawlessnesses/transgressions
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the transgressions of the servants of God" (EMET/LOGOS). "Transgressions" is more precise for *anomiai* = lawless acts.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 59:2 "the absence of the master is the time remaining before his coming"

- **EMET:** "the absence of the master is the time remaining before his coming"
- **LOGOS:** "the absence of the master is the time remaining before his coming"
- **PNEUMA:** "the master's absence represents the remaining time before he comes"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree exactly.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the absence of the master is the time remaining before his coming." The eschatological calculation is crisp.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 59:3 "could I then have perceived these things?" vs. "could I have perceived them by myself?"

- **EMET:** "could I then have perceived these things?"
- **LOGOS:** "could I have perceived them by myself?"
- **PNEUMA:** "could I have ever figured this out on my own?"
- **Greek:** *ēdunamēn tauta gnōnai* — was I able to know/perceive these things?
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "could I have perceived them by myself?" (LOGOS). Adding "by myself" makes Hermas's self-deprecating question more pointed.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 59:3 "no man who has God in his heart" vs. "no one who has God in his heart"

- **EMET:** "no man who has God in his heart"
- **LOGOS:** "no one who has God in his heart"
- **PNEUMA:** "anyone who truly has God in their heart"
- **Greek:** *oudeis...ho echōn ton theon en tē kardia* — no one who has God in his heart
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "no one who has God in his heart" (LOGOS). "No one" is appropriately universal; PNEUMA's "truly" adds intensity not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 59:4 "friends are the holy prophets who served God" vs. "friends are the prophets"

- **EMET:** "the friends are the prophets who served God"
- **LOGOS:** "the friends are the holy prophets who served God"
- **PNEUMA:** "the friends are the holy prophets who served God"
- **Note:** Only EMET omits "holy"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the friends are the holy prophets who served God" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The adjective "holy" (*hoi hagioi prophetai*) should be preserved.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 59.*
